body_markdown:
A SaaS payment setup should help customers start a trial, pay again and move to the right plan as their needs change. Razorpay Subscriptions brings customer authorisation and recurring collections together through supported cards, UPI AutoPay and eMandate, with international recurring-card payments available to eligible accounts. It is a strong fit for Indian SaaS businesses that want these billing flows in one subscription product and can design plan changes around the supported payment-method rules.


## Key takeaways


- Start with the billing journey you need at low volume, then review payment mix and commercial terms as GMV grows. Compare processing fees, subscription charges, taxes and optional services as a complete cost model.
- Offer a trial using a[future subscription start date](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/create) , with the required customer authentication completed upfront.
- Give customers a clear upgrade journey with[Razorpay’s card subscription update flow](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/update) . Eligible immediate updates calculate proration. Domestic-card subscriptions support linked-offer changes at cycle end; UPI AutoPay and eMandate subscriptions do not support in-place updates.
- Use supported international cards and currencies for overseas subscriptions, with INR settlement. Domestic UPI AutoPay and eMandate collections use INR; confirm activation for each required flow.


## How should a SaaS business plan trials, upgrades and billing as it grows?


Razorpay Subscriptions supports trial-to-paid billing and eligible card-subscription changes. Set a[future billing date](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/create) after customer authentication to offer a trial, and use the supported card-update flow for prorated charges or refunds. Domestic-card subscriptions support linked-offer changes at cycle end. UPI AutoPay and eMandate continue recurring collections on their existing terms and do not support in-place updates.


For a low-volume launch, select the billing flows your customers need and calculate their full cost using your commercial terms. Revisit payment mix and costs as GMV grows. Eligible international recurring-card collections settle in INR. Razorpay fits businesses that can connect these documented collection flows to their planned customer journey.


## Build a complete SaaS payment-cost model


The right cost comparison connects what you pay with the billing work your business needs to do. Evaluate Razorpay’s recurring collections, trial setup and supported international-card flow alongside payment-processing fees, subscription-product charges where applicable, taxes and optional faster settlements. Use your actual payment mix and commercial terms to compare the complete workflow, rather than treating a headline processing rate as the full cost.


Cost or outcome What to include


Payment processing Rates for each enabled payment method and international flow.


Recurring billing Subscriptions charges under your account terms.


Optional services Charges for routing, accelerated settlement or other selected products.


Taxes and invoicing Applicable taxes and the charges shown in your quotation and invoice.


Operating costs Engineering, reconciliation, customer communication and billing support.


Renewal outcomes Successful renewals, failed payments, cancellations and recovered payments, tracked separately.


Use[Razorpay pricing](https://razorpay.com/pricing) as a starting point, then apply the rates and product scope agreed for your account. Include an introductory offer’s eligibility, duration and post-offer rate in your forecast.


## Offer recurring billing and a trial period


A trial gives customers time to experience the product before regular billing starts. With Razorpay, you can create that period by[setting the subscription’s start date in the future](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/create) . The customer completes the required authentication upfront, and scheduled billing begins on the selected date. Make the trial end date, renewal amount and cancellation process clear.


For upgrades, use the[documented subscription-update rules](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/update) : prorated changes apply to supported card flows, while domestic-card, UPI AutoPay and eMandate subscriptions have method-specific restrictions. Match the upgrade journey to those rules before launch.


## Plan upgrades and proration around the payment method


Razorpay supports plan changes and proration through eligible card subscription updates. The supported journey depends on the payment method:


Billing journey Razorpay approach


Introduce a new plan or price Create a new Plan, or duplicate and modify one; existing Plans remain unchanged.


Apply an eligible immediate card-subscription update Calculate the prorated charge or refund through the documented update flow. The subscription must be authenticated or active.


Update a domestic-card subscription Change the linked offer at the end of the billing cycle. Other in-place plan, quantity or duration changes are not supported for this flow.


Collect with UPI AutoPay or eMandate Continue recurring collections on the existing subscription terms. In-place subscription updates are not supported.


Use the[update guide](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/update) and[Subscriptions FAQs](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs) when designing the journey. A change outside the supported update flow needs a separately designed customer-authorisation and subscription workflow.


## Launch at low volume and expand with demand


For an early-stage SaaS business, a focused launch can start with one billing interval, the payment methods your customers need and a clear trial-to-paid journey. Estimate costs using your expected transaction volume and account terms, then review the mix as you grow.


Add international billing, further plans or optional payment products when the business case supports them. This keeps implementation effort tied to actual customer demand. Review product eligibility, pricing and operating requirements at each stage.


## Build a dependable billing workflow


1. Define the plan, billing interval, trial period and payment method.
2. Complete customer authorisation and record the subscription identifier.
3. Process the documented subscription and payment status events in your application.
4. Set access rules for successful renewals, pending payments and cancellations.
5. Use the documented method-specific retry behaviour and give customers a clear way to resolve a payment issue.
6. Test supported updates, cancellation and reconciliation before launch.


Follow the[Subscriptions documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions) for integration details. Evaluate[Optimizer](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/optimizer) separately if your payment mix calls for gateway routing, and measure renewal outcomes for your own customer cohort.


## Reach international subscription customers


For an eligible Indian merchant account, Razorpay Subscriptions supports card payments in supported international currencies. The Subscriptions FAQs state that settlements are made in INR. UPI payments do not support international currencies.


Confirm the account’s international recurring-card configuration, supported currency and charges before launch. See the[international-subscription guide](https://razorpay.com/blog/international-subscriptions-india) for the setup decisions.


## Calculate payment and operating costs clearly


**Blended payment-cost rate = payment-related fees and applicable taxes for the period ÷ successfully processed payment value for the same period × 100.**


Use a consistent accounting basis and state how tax credits, refunds and reversals are treated. Track engineering and support costs separately, alongside renewal and recovery outcomes.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can I offer a free trial with Razorpay Subscriptions?


Yes. Set a future billing start date when creating the subscription. The customer completes the required authentication upfront, and scheduled billing starts on that date. Account and payment-processing terms still apply.


### How should a low-volume SaaS business start?


Choose the recurring methods and billing interval your customers need, set up authorisation and renewal events, and test the trial-to-paid journey. Build your cost forecast from your account’s processing and Subscriptions terms.


### How do I support upgrades and proration?


Razorpay supports prorated changes for eligible immediate card-subscription updates. Domestic-card subscriptions support linked-offer changes at cycle end. UPI AutoPay and eMandate support recurring collections on their existing terms and do not support in-place updates. Choose the billing journey by payment method using the[update guide](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/update) .


### How should I compare SaaS payment pricing?


Include payment processing, Subscriptions, selected optional products, applicable taxes and operating work. Compare these costs with measured renewal outcomes for your business.


### What should I test before launching a new subscription plan?


Test authorisation, trial completion, successful and failed renewal events, supported changes, cancellation, customer communication and reconciliation for each enabled method.
